warning: A6 is exploratory model-zoo evidence at n=1,000 on a single partition. It is not a promotion study and does not supersede A2's 36-fold historical validation. No model here is PROMOTED, and the paper-trading engine remains fail-closed.

metric_notes.smape: sMAPE is not reported as a headline metric: the target is a signed log return that crosses zero, so its denominator |actual| + |forecast| vanishes on quiet days and the statistic saturates near 200% for every model in the zoo -- including the naive baseline, which scores exactly 200%. It is computed and retained per model for inspection, not ranked on.
metric_notes.directional_accuracy: a forecast of exactly zero is scored as wrong rather than half-right; three baselines forecast a constant and one forecasts exactly zero, and crediting the tie would hand it a free 50%. Balanced accuracy and MCC are reported beside it.
metric_notes.directional_null: tested against the training-chosen constant direction, not against 0.5. This series has roughly a 53% up-day base rate, so always saying up beats a coin while containing no information.

registry_entries.description: AdaBoost.R2 over depth-3 stumps, 200 rounds at lr=0.05.
notes: Reweights toward hard examples, which on this series are largely noise -- a hypothesis worth testing rather than assuming.

registry_entries.description: AR(3) on log returns, evaluated by the frozen linear recursion.
notes: Lag order chosen from {1, 3, 7} on DEV only.

registry_entries.description: ARIMA(1,0,1) with constant on log returns; d=0 because the series is already differenced.
notes: Order chosen from {(1,0,0), (1,0,1), (2,0,2)} on DEV only.

registry_entries.description: Ridge with the penalty inferred by evidence approximation.
notes: A control on how much the frozen alphas cost the other linear models.

registry_entries.description: Two causal convolutions (kernel 3) and a mean over time.
notes: Fixed five-bar receptive field.

Trained on the numpy autodiff engine in this repository, whose gradients are checked against central finite differences. torch is not a dependency: the lock is compiled with --all-extras and installed by the fresh-clone CI job, so a torch extra would put a multi-gigabyte CUDA closure in every clean install.
Budget frozen and shared across all seven: lookback 24, max 60 epochs, batch 64, lr 0.003, patience 8, seed 20260909. Early stopping watches DEV.

registry_entries.description: Ridge with split-conformal intervals calibrated on the DEV block.
notes: The conformal coverage guarantee requires exchangeability, which a volatility-clustered daily return series does not satisfy. The nominal level is reported as nominal and the empirical coverage is measured; the gap between them is the result.
Calibrated on DEV, never on HOLDOUT -- calibrating on the block it is about to be scored against would guarantee coverage by construction and measure nothing.
Uses signed residual quantiles rather than absolute ones, so an asymmetric return distribution produces an asymmetric interval.

registry_entries.description: Single regression tree, max_depth=4, min_samples_leaf=20.
notes: The interpretable control the ensembles are measured against.

registry_entries.description: EGARCH(1,1,1) with Student-t innovations: log-variance with a leverage term.
notes: Forecasts conditional variance, not direction. Its POINT output is the fitted constant mean and will score like the naive baseline; that is the honest answer, not a failure.
Quantiles come from the fitted Student-t conditional distribution, so they are the model's own statement rather than a Gaussian assumption added afterwards.

registry_entries.description: L1+L2 penalty at a 0.5 mix ratio.
300 extremely randomised trees at the shared ceiling.
notes: Random split thresholds: more variance reduction, more bias.

registry_entries.description: Symmetric GARCH(1,1) with Student-t innovations on percent log returns.
notes: Forecasts conditional variance, not direction. Its POINT output is the fitted constant mean and will score like the naive baseline; that is the honest answer, not a failure.
Quantiles come from the fitted Student-t conditional distribution, so they are the model's own statement rather than a Gaussian assumption added afterwards.

registry_entries.description: GJR-GARCH(1,1,1) with Student-t innovations: threshold asymmetry in levels.
notes: Forecasts conditional variance, not direction. Its POINT output is the fitted constant mean and will score like the naive baseline; that is the honest answer, not a failure.

registry_entries.description: Stagewise gradient boosting, 300 rounds at lr=0.03, subsample 0.8.
GRU over the 24-step window; last hidden state projected to a scalar.
notes: Trained on the numpy autodiff engine in this repository, whose gradients are checked against central finite differences. torch is not a dependency: the lock is compiled with --all-extras and installed by the fresh-clone CI job, so a torch extra would put a multi-gigabyte CUDA closure in every clean install.
Budget frozen and shared across all seven: lookback 24, max 60 epochs, batch 64, lr 0.003, patience 8, seed 20260909. Early stopping watches DEV.

registry_entries.description: Histogram-binned gradient boosting, 300 iterations, early stopping off.
notes: Its advantage is speed at large n, which this lab does not have; it is here to check the binning approximation costs nothing at n=1,000.

registry_entries.description: log(1 + mean training simple return).
notes: Distinct from random_walk_drift by Jensen's inequality: the arithmetic mean of simple returns exceeds the mean log return by approximately half the return variance.

registry_entries.description: Damped Holt linear trend on log price, innovations state-space form.
Holt-Winters additive seasonal exponential smoothing at period 7.
registry_entries.unsuitable_reason: no weekly seasonality in the training rows: ACF(7) = -0.018 against a +/-0.062 white-noise band, day-of-week ANOVA p = 0.95, STL seasonal strength 0.065. A seasonal component here would fit noise, and at n=1,000 it would fit it confidently.
notes: Registered rather than omitted: the measurement that excludes it is itself a result, and a missing row is indistinguishable from an oversight.

registry_entries.description: Huber loss: squared inside epsilon, absolute outside.
notes: Included specifically because daily crypto returns carry real outliers.

registry_entries.description: Distance-weighted 25-NN on standardised causal features.
notes: Meaningful because the features are approximately stationary -- lagged returns and rolling statistics, not raw prices -- so Euclidean distance is a defensible statement that two days looked alike.
Limited by dimensionality: 11 features and 1,000 points is sparse, and 'nearest' begins to mean 'least far'. The distance to the k-th training neighbour is reported so that is visible as a number.
Limited by temporal correlation: adjacent rows share rolling windows, so a query's neighbours are often its calendar neighbours, which inflates similarity without adding independent evidence.
Fits nothing and stores everything, so it reports no parameter count rather than reporting the size of the training set.

registry_entries.description: L1-penalised least squares; reports which features survived.
notes: At n=1,000 which coefficients survive is more informative than the MAE.

registry_entries.description: Epsilon-insensitive linear SVR.
Stochastic local level on log price; the state-space form of simple exponential smoothing.
notes: Estimated by maximum likelihood over state variances, via the Kalman filter. Kalman is not registered as a separate model because it is the estimator for this family, not a model.

registry_entries.description: Stochastic local linear trend on log price; the state-space form of Holt's method.
notes: Shares its structure with holt_linear_trend and differs in estimation: variances by likelihood here, smoothing weights there. Two entries, one structure, different forecasts.

registry_entries.description: LSTM with forget-gate bias initialised to 1.0.
notes: Registered beside the GRU because the extra gate is the hypothesis: at 977 sequences the parameters may cost more than the memory buys.

registry_entries.description: Gradient boosting on pinball loss, one model per quantile level.
notes: Estimates conditional quantiles. Not a confidence interval and it carries no coverage guarantee; calibration is measured, not claimed.
Its point forecast is the conditional median, because that is what pinball loss at 0.5 estimates. It has no mean to report.
Independently fitted quantiles can cross; the columns are sorted, which cannot hurt calibration because a crossed pair is a statement the model could not have meant.

registry_entries.description: Koenker-Bassett linear quantile regression, one fit per level.
notes: The linear control for quantile_gbr: same loss, same levels, no capacity to fit a non-linear conditional distribution.

registry_entries.description: 300 bagged trees at the shared capacity ceiling.
notes: Capacity frozen for n=1,000; an unbounded forest reaches training R^2 ~ 1 and evaluation skill ~ 0, and that gap is the lesson.

registry_entries.description: Constant drift: the mean training log return.
notes: Mathematically identical to the classical endpoint drift (log P_end - log P_start) / (n - 1), because log returns telescope. Registered once rather than twice.
A2's strongest model over 36 folds, at MAE skill +0.003957 -- which was still a REJECT.

sample_efficiency.purpose: whether the ranking is stable in n; explicitly not a basis for choosing a model

comparison.note: a raw p-value below alpha in a family this size is expected; the q-value is what a claim should rest on

diversity.interpretation: high error correlation with high sign agreement means the zoo is one model wearing forty names, and an ensemble would add nothing. This is measured here so a future ensemble study starts from evidence rather than from optimism. A6 builds no ensemble.
